source: Schaafstal, Schraagen & van Berlo (2000) Cognitive task analysis and innovation of training: the case of structured troubleshooting
finding: Founding applied study. Two observational studies of real troubleshooting plus a literature review gave a cognitive task analysis. From it the authors built 'structured troubleshooting': one general strategy plus a multilevel functional breakdown of each system. Trained technicians fixed about twice as many malfunctions, in less time, than traditionally trained ones.
numbers: About 2x malfunctions solved; less time; less training time; 2 preliminary observational studies. Exact N, error rates and test statistics not seen (full text paywalled).
limits: Only the abstract page was read (UTwente and PubMed). Navy radar setting. No independent replication found in this pass. Effect size unknown.
agent_relevance: Strongest field evidence that an explicit, general diagnostic cycle plus a system map beats content-only training. Supports giving the agent a fixed cycle (S1-S4) and a system breakdown.

source: Schaafstal, Schraagen & van Berlo (2000) Cognitive task analysis and innovation of training: the case of structured troubleshooting
finding: PubMed abstract confirms: the method needed less training time and gave a more explicit, uniform approach. Authors claim it cuts training and troubleshooting cost.
numbers: Vol 42(1), pp 75-86. About 89 Scopus citations on the UTwente page.
limits: Abstract only. The cost-saving claim is the authors', not measured in what I read.
agent_relevance: The gain came from method, not from more domain knowledge. A scaffold can supply the method.

source: Dounas-Frazer et al. (2016) Investigating the role of model-based reasoning while troubleshooting an electric circuit
finding: Gives the Schaafstal four-task cycle: Formulate Problem Description, Generate Causes, Test, Repair and Evaluate. The process is recursive and nonlinear. Test asks 'is the proposed cause an actual fault?'. Repair and Evaluate asks 'is the apparatus functioning as expected?'. A failed repair sends the troubleshooter back to Generate Causes.
numbers: 4 tasks; loops: refuted cause -> new cause; failed repair -> new cause (missed fault or multiple faults).
limits: Secondary account of Schaafstal 2000 (p. 79) and Jonassen and Hung 2006, read through a citing paper, not the originals.
agent_relevance: Direct map to S1 (describe), S2 (causes), S3 (test), S4 (repair and verify) with loop-back edges. The verify step is mandatory (G3).

source: Dounas-Frazer et al. (2016) Investigating the role of model-based reasoning while troubleshooting an electric circuit
finding: Generate Causes works two ways. Experts recognise symptoms from experience. Anyone meeting a problem for the first time reasons from function, causal thinking and documents.
numbers: Attributed to Schaafstal et al.; no numbers.
limits: Second-hand summary of the expert/novice split. The recognition route fails on novel faults.
agent_relevance: Agent should try recall of known symptom-cause pairs first, then fall back to functional reasoning when recall is absent or the test refutes it.

source: Dounas-Frazer et al. (2016) Investigating the role of model-based reasoning while troubleshooting an electric circuit
finding: Six knowledge types support troubleshooting: Domain, System, Procedural, Strategic, Metacognitive, Experiential (from Jonassen and Hung 2006 and Van Gog). Strategic and metacognitive knowledge are not shown in the modeling framework; they sit in the transitions between phases.
numbers: 6 types.
limits: Taxonomy, not tested as six separate factors.
agent_relevance: Map to schema: domain/system = context given; procedural = tools; strategic = operators; metacognitive = impasse detector; experiential = case memory.

source: Dounas-Frazer et al. (2016) Investigating the role of model-based reasoning while troubleshooting an electric circuit
finding: Three named search strategies: Exhaustive (list all faults, test one by one), Topographic (follow the signal path upstream or downstream), Split-Half (test the midpoint, keep the bad half).
numbers: 3 strategies, from Jonassen and Hung 2006.
limits: Descriptions only. No efficiency comparison among them in this source.
agent_relevance: Split-half is binary search over a system map. It needs a hierarchical system model first. Cheap to implement as a code-controlled operator.

source: Dounas-Frazer et al. (2016) Investigating the role of model-based reasoning while troubleshooting an electric circuit
finding: Think-aloud study of 8 student pairs (4 at CU Boulder, 4 at Maine) diagnosing a two-fault cascade amplifier. All 8 pairs went through all four tasks. Most moved from Formulate to Generate about halfway. Testing ran almost continuously. Repairs came in short bursts.
numbers: N=8 pairs; 2-minute interval coding; 2 faults (R3=100 ohm instead of 1k; burned-out op-amp).
limits: Physics majors in pairs, one circuit, qualitative coding, no outcome comparison. Not a test of the theory's predictions.
agent_relevance: The four-task cycle describes real behaviour, but with overlap and no clean order. The scaffold should allow loops, not a strict line.

source: Dounas-Frazer et al. (2016) Investigating the role of model-based reasoning while troubleshooting an electric circuit
finding: Strategies seen: 5 of 8 pairs used Split-Half. Each of those 5 built a two-subsystem model, predicted each stage's output, compared, and isolated Stage 2. Pairs A and B used an Exhaustive replace-both-op-amps move after checking wiring and resistors.
numbers: 5/8 Split-Half; 5/5 model construction, prediction, comparison; 2/5 proposal at isolation.
limits: Small N. Coding by the authors; no inter-rater statistic seen in the text I read.
agent_relevance: Split-half needs a prediction first. The agent should state the expected value at a test point before measuring.

source: Dounas-Frazer et al. (2016) Investigating the role of model-based reasoning while troubleshooting an electric circuit
finding: All 8 pairs fixed the 100-ohm resistor. 7 of 8 pairs found and replaced the faulty op-amp. 5 of 8 pairs made needless or wrong changes (replacing R1, rewiring from a bad schematic mapping, replacing the working Stage 1 op-amp).
numbers: 8/8 resistor; 7/8 op-amp; 5/8 wrong or needless revisions; pairs A-C replaced the Stage 1 op-amp.
limits: Recall of past experience ('last time it was a bad op-amp') drove one pair's swap.
agent_relevance: Recall is fast but can cause needless repairs. Require a test that the swapped part was bad, and an evaluative check after repair.

source: Dounas-Frazer et al. (2016) Investigating the role of model-based reasoning while troubleshooting an electric circuit
finding: Three measurement kinds map to tasks: formative (build the problem description), diagnostic (test a cause), evaluative (check the repair).
numbers: 3 measurement types.
limits: The authors' own coding addition, not Schaafstal's.
agent_relevance: Label each probe by purpose. Evaluative probes are the verification gate; formative probes must not be mistaken for tests.

source: Dounas-Frazer et al. (2015) The role of modeling in troubleshooting: an example from electronics
finding: Pilot of the same interviews: 4 pairs from each of two institutions, 16 students total, 25-60 minute interviews. Split-Half was used once the model of two subsystems existed; without that model a student could not make a prediction.
numbers: 16 students; 8 pairs; 25-60 min; total gain -20.
limits: One illustrative episode of about 90 seconds. Qualitative.
agent_relevance: Model construction comes before prediction, prediction before comparison. Matches S1 then S3.

source: Dounas-Frazer, Van De Bogart, Stetzer, Lewandowski (2017) Socially mediated metacognition during collaborative troubleshooting
finding: Pairs showed shared monitoring in four episodes: planning a strategy, first sight of the wrong output, split-half isolation, and deciding what to replace. Clusters of metacognitive talk were most frequent right after measurements of the whole circuit or the first subsystem.
numbers: 8 pairs; 4 episode types; 3 pairs had all four, 5 had three.
limits: Not designed to compare pair quality. Exploratory.
agent_relevance: The control points are the moments right after new evidence arrives. Fits G1: doubt only on a signal.

source: Dounas-Frazer & Lewandowski (2016) Electronics lab instructors' approaches to troubleshooting instruction
finding: 20 instructors from 18 institutions. Nearly all valued troubleshooting. About half did not assess it; the others used idiosyncratic assessments. About half said part of the skill is innate. Instructors most often named forward-topographic and split-half strategies.
numbers: N=20 instructors, 18 institutions, 31-question interview.
limits: Self-report, not performance. Shows the field has no standard test.
agent_relevance: With no agreed benchmark, we need our own checks of the diagnostic cycle.

source: Dounas-Frazer & Lewandowski (2016) Nothing works the first time: an expert experimental physics epistemology
finding: Expert belief: things do not work the first time, so faults are normal and must be expected. This shapes how experts teach and expect troubleshooting.
numbers: Same 20 interviews.
limits: Epistemology claim from interviews.
agent_relevance: Expect the first attempt to fail. A prior of failure supports test-and-repair loops.

source: Dounas-Frazer et al. (2018) Pathways to proposing causes for unexpected experimental results
finding: Some students did not propose a cause at the first discrepancy. They kept measuring and revising until a cause emerged. This pathway was not in the modeling framework.
numbers: 10 think-aloud interviews with CU Boulder students; 2 episodes shown.
limits: Two case episodes only.
agent_relevance: Do not force a cause hypothesis early. Allow more observation before Generate Causes.

source: Dounas-Frazer et al. (2015) The role of metacognition in troubleshooting: an example from electronics
finding: Cites Schaafstal: a standard course on content understanding did not prepare Navy students to troubleshoot radar, but adding structured troubleshooting gave significant gains.
numbers: Not stated here.
limits: Second-hand claim; no numbers.
agent_relevance: A second route to the same Schaafstal result: the content-versus-method point.

source: Jonassen & Hung (2006) Learning to troubleshoot (secondary blog note)
finding: Note of the model: construct problem space; identify fault systems; diagnose; generate and verify solutions; remember the experience. Four hypothesis levels: system, subsystem, device, component. Proposed design is a case library of prior troubleshooting stories.
numbers: 5 steps; 4 levels; no empirical data in the note.
limits: Blog note of the paper, not the paper. The note's author doubts the four-level split matters; the skill is drill-down.
agent_relevance: Step 5, remember the experience, is the memory write. The case library maps to an experiential store.

source: Jonassen & Hung (2006) Educational Psychology Review 18(1) 77-114
finding: Could not open (redirect to login). Facts above come from citing papers. Claimed: troubleshooting is problem solving where the goal state is known but the needed information is not; earlier methods failed to give transferable skill; the paper proposes a model, a learning environment and a case library.
numbers: Pages 77-114.
limits: Not read. Do not quote exact numbers from it.
agent_relevance: Needs a second pass when access exists.

source: Schaafstal & Schraagen (1993) Training of systematic diagnosis: a case study in electronics troubleshooting (AI-ED 1993)
finding: Named in a search result only (pp 529-533). Early version of the structured-troubleshooting idea.
numbers: none
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Check later.

source: Rasmussen (1983) Skills, rules, and knowledge
finding: Three levels of control: skill (signals), rule (signs), knowledge (symbols, mental model). Fault diagnosis is a knowledge-based task. Knowledge-based control is slow and used only when rules fail. Boundaries between levels shift with training.
numbers: 3 levels; theory paper, no experiment; read via a teaching summary.
limits: Secondary page; it did not discuss topographic versus symptomatic search.
agent_relevance: Matches G1: use fast known-rule recall first, switch to slow model-based search only on an impasse.

source: Johnson (1988) Cognitive analysis of expert and novice troubleshooting performance (Performance Improvement Quarterly 1, 38-54)
finding: Cited as the source that experts use ordered operations that cut the number of possible fault locations.
numbers: none
limits: Seen only in reference lists.
agent_relevance: Check for numbers.

source: Van Gog, Paas, van Merrienboer (2005) Uncovering expertise-related differences in troubleshooting (Appl Cogn Psychol 19, 205-221)
finding: Cited for orienting to the circuit and expert-novice differences using eye movements and verbal protocols. Paywalled.
numbers: none
limits: Reference list only.
agent_relevance: Candidate for round two.

source: Van Gog et al. (2006, 2008) process-oriented worked examples for troubleshooting transfer (Learning and Instruction 16, 18)
finding: Cited as showing that worked examples of the process help transfer in circuit troubleshooting.
numbers: none
limits: Reference list only.
agent_relevance: Support for showing the agent worked diagnostic traces.

source: Uncertainty of Thoughts: uncertainty-aware planning enhances information seeking in LLMs (2024)
finding: An LLM asks questions to find a fault. UoT picks the question with the best expected information gain over a set of possible faults. On troubleshooting (FloDial, 894 dialogues, 153 faults, max 20 turns), GPT-4 success rose from 43.7% to 67.3% with UoT in the closed-set setting; mean turns in successes 7.8.
numbers: SR 43.7 -> 67.3 (GPT-4, troubleshooting); average +38.1% across 5 datasets and 5 LLMs; +46.6% for Llama3-70B; beats CoT-SC by 33.8% and Reflexion by 29.9%.
limits: The simulated user is GPT-4; fault set given up front in the closed setting. Not real devices.
agent_relevance: Split-half as expected information gain. Question choice by code over a candidate set fits G5.

source: FaulT-Bench: network troubleshooting agents under unreliable user tickets (2026)
finding: On accurate tickets (80 scenarios) agents score 0.912 (SADE), 0.942 (Claude Code baseline), 0.941 (ReAct): nearly solved. On 72 healthy networks with a false ticket the mean is 0.820. Over-diagnosis (reporting a fault that is not there) occurred in 24% (51/210), 16% (33/209) and 11% (21/198) of answered runs.
numbers: 200 scenarios, 8 topologies; wrong-device 0.957, wrong-cause 0.911; naive no-detail persona 0.497 mean (Claude Code 0.283).
limits: Emulated networks; authors' own scoring; 8% of cells moved by 0.5 or more between passes.
agent_relevance: Agents lack a criterion to conclude 'no fault'. The verify step must allow 'no fault found'. The skills that help find faults raise false alarms.

source: LLM-as-an-Investigator: evidence-first agentic reasoning for interactive problem diagnosis (2026)
finding: Agent keeps competing hypotheses, asks discriminating questions, adds a counterfactual critic and a final adjudicator. Ablations on 303 forum threads: full system final 79.2, potential 89.2. Without structured investigation 72.8; without counterfactual critique 74.0; without follow-up questions 75.0; without hypothesis expansion 76.5 (potential 79.3); without adjudication 76.0; without weight updates 78.5.
numbers: 303 threads; mechanical, electrical, hydraulic; the user's wrong cause was chosen in 2 of 10 challenged cases.
limits: Authors' own judge; simulated user; the part of the paper I read did not cite Schaafstal or Jonassen.
agent_relevance: Generating candidates matters more than selecting among them. Matches S2 breadth then S3 testing.

source: NIKA: a network arena for benchmarking AI agents on network troubleshooting (2025)
finding: Public benchmark: 54 network issues across 5 scenarios giving 640 distinct tasks, 30+ MCP tools, and more than 900 released reasoning traces.
numbers: 54 issues; 640 tasks; 900+ traces.
limits: Benchmark paper; the agent comparison was not read in detail.
agent_relevance: Possible external test set for the diagnostic cycle.

source: Evaluating LLMs' effectiveness on real-world consumer device repair questions (2026)
finding: Abstract page only: 991 real repair questions from Reddit with technician reference answers; six LLMs in English and Bangla; GPT-5.4 best. Scores not given in the abstract.
numbers: 991 questions; 6 models.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence; leave to the LLM angle.
